content.value_statement: Difficult feedback conversations often become vague, defensive, or poorly documented. This skill provides structured scripts and frameworks for clear, respectful workplace feedback.
actual_capabilities: Guides preparation, delivery, and follow-up for difficult conversations.
Formats feedback with Situation, Behavior, and Impact statements.
Provides scripts for defensiveness, denial, emotion, deflection, and counter-attack.
Helps reset stakeholder expectations around scope, timeline, and ownership.
Creates follow-up messages, check-in plans, and action summaries.
limitations: It provides communication guidance, not legal or HR compliance advice.
It cannot verify facts without user-provided workplace context.
It does not replace manager judgment or formal performance processes.
It may need adaptation for company policy, local law, and culture.

use_cases.title: Address Team Performance Issues
use_cases.description: Prepare a specific, respectful conversation about missed deadlines, code quality, or engagement issues.

use_cases.title: Give Peer Feedback
use_cases.description: Turn observations into SBI feedback for peers without using blame or assumptions.

use_cases.title: Reset Project Expectations
use_cases.description: Push back on unrealistic timelines by presenting trade-offs and documenting agreement.

prompt_templates.title: Draft SBI Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to give feedback about [behavior]. Ask for missing context, then draft a Situation-Behavior-Impact statement.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Difficult Conversation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare for a difficult conversation about [issue]. Create a preparation, delivery, and follow-up plan.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Defensive Response
prompt_templates.prompt: The person may respond defensively about [topic]. Draft calm responses that keep the discussion specific and constructive.

prompt_templates.title: Reset Stakeholder Expectations
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me push back on [deadline or scope request]. Present trade-offs, options, risks, and a written follow-up summary.

output_examples.input: A peer interrupts others during sprint planning.
output_examples.output: Situation: In yesterday's sprint planning. Behavior: You interrupted two teammates while they explained estimates. Impact: We lost detail and some concerns were not discussed.

output_examples.input: A developer submits pull requests with missing tests.
output_examples.output: Opening: I noticed the last two pull requests had no unit tests. I want to understand what is making testing difficult and how I can help.

output_examples.input: A stakeholder asks for a large feature by month end.
output_examples.output: Response: We can meet that date with a smaller first release, or deliver the full scope later. I recommend choosing the first option and documenting the trade-off.

best_practices: Gather specific examples before drafting feedback.
Separate observable behavior from assumptions about intent.
End each conversation with clear actions and a check-in date.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to script accusations or personal attacks.
Do not present feedback without checking facts and context.
Do not treat the output as legal, HR, or disciplinary advice.

faq.question: Can this skill help with positive feedback?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses SBI for both recognition and constructive feedback.

faq.question: Does it work outside software teams?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples focus on software teams, but the frameworks apply to many professional settings.

faq.question: Can it write a complete conversation script?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the situation, behavior, impact, and desired outcome for a stronger script.

faq.question: Does it replace HR guidance?
faq.answer: No. Use HR or legal guidance for formal discipline, protected issues, or policy questions.

faq.question: Can it help when someone gets defensive?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes calm responses for defensiveness, denial, emotion, deflection, and counter-attack.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the context, observed behavior, impact, relationship, desired outcome, and any company constraints.
